title: Customer rollout plan for Runtime LTS pilot (cohort, success criteria, support readiness, comms cadence)
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
Context
- We are launching the first Runtime LTS pilot (runtime-1.20-lts.*) to a small set of enterprise customers to validate: (1) slower-change promise, (2) backport workflow, (3) Private/Dedicated upgrade + rollback flows, and (4) enterprise-grade release notes/comms.
- This ticket defines who is in the pilot, what “success” means, how Support/SRE/Release Eng are prepared, and what communication cadence we commit to.

Goals
1) Pilot cohort selection: identify 3–6 accounts (mix of Private/VPC + Dedicated) and document why they’re included.
2) Success criteria: define measurable and subjective criteria (upgrade pain reduction, incident rate, release note quality, operational confidence).
3) Support readiness: escalation path + artifacts required before customers receive LTS bits.
4) Comms cadence: define pre-announce, release-day, and post-release communications (including who sends, channel, and SLA for acknowledgements).

Non-goals
- Defining the LTS branching model/backport policy (covered by Runtime + Release Eng docs / ADR).
- Expanding pilot beyond the initial cohort until we hit success criteria and SRE signs off.

Pilot cohort (proposed)
Note: use internal account IDs and keep comms under NDA. Final list to be confirmed with Sales/CS and Support capacity.

Tier 0 (design partners / highest urgency)
- Account 55291 (Private deployment): ongoing stability concerns and explicit “stable runtime line” ask. Source: sources/hubspot/account_55291_private-deployment-lts-notes.json
- Deal 118203 (Enterprise requirement): “Runtime LTS channel” called out as close requirement / renewal risk. Source: sources/hubspot/deal_118203_enterprise-lts-requirement.json

Tier 1 (upgrade pain + recent regression)
- SUP-3921 (Private deployment LTS request): requested timeline + environment details; good candidate for validating Private installer flow and rollback. Source: sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-3921.json
- SUP-3950 (runtime regression post-upgrade): strong signal for why LTS exists; candidate for validating backport policy and risk communication. Source: sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-3950.json

Tier 2 (release notes / process feedback)
- SUP-3988 (release notes too noisy): candidate for validating “enterprise-style” LTS release notes template and risk tags. Source: sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-3988.json

Cohort size / mix
- Target: 4 accounts total for pilot launch
  - 2x Private (incl. at least 1 on-prem or restricted VPC)
  - 1x Dedicated capacity customer
  - 1x “hybrid” customer using Hosted for dev + Private for prod (if available via CS)
- Rationale: exercise both artifact distribution paths and operational procedures.

Entry criteria for an account
- Has a named technical owner on customer side (can participate in upgrade window + feedback).
- Has an established support channel (ticketing + named CS contact) and willingness to run a planned maintenance window.
- Agrees to: (a) provide baseline metrics (latency/error rate), (b) participate in 30-min weekly check-in for first 4 weeks, (c) accept limited scope of backports per policy.

Exit criteria / graduation
- Account can remain on LTS if they (a) successfully upgraded, (b) can consume patch releases, and (c) acknowledges LTS limitations (no feature asks via LTS).

Success criteria (pilot-level)
Operational
- 100% of pilot customers successfully install/upgrade to runtime-1.20-lts.0 (or .1) using supported path.
- Rollback works as documented for at least 1 customer exercise (planned rollback drill or real rollback if needed).
- No Severity-1 incidents attributable to the LTS release process/artifact integrity.
- Patch release execution: ≤ 5 business days from “backport approved” to “patch published” for at least 1 real backport.

Reliability / performance (as measured by SRE gates + customer reported)
- No statistically significant regression vs customer’s pre-upgrade baseline outside defined gates (p95/p99 latency thresholds and error-rate budgets as per SRE doc).
- Any observed degradation has: (a) documented mitigations in release notes, (b) clear rollback guidance, and (c) owner assigned within 1 business day.

Customer experience
- Release notes rated “useful” by at least 3/4 pilot customers (qualitative survey) with specific callouts: risk level, behavior changes, mitigations, upgrade steps.
- Support sentiment: Support/CS reports lower churn from “forced upgrade” requests (compare number of escalations on runtime upgrades pre vs post pilot window).

Support readiness (must be true before external rollout)
Artifacts
- LTS overview + how to request backports (internal + customer-safe summary). Source: Confluence Runtime LTS channel overview (to be linked when published)
- LTS release notes template finalized and used for runtime-1.20-lts.0. Dependency: PM-812 + ENG-4826
- Private upgrade/rollback guide aligned to LTS versioning and artifact locations. Dependency: ENG-4829
- Change management + comms templates approved (Product + Support + SRE). Source: enterprise-runtime-lts-change-management (Confluence)
- Support internal KB: “Runtime LTS intake checklist” (what data to request, which team to page, expected timelines)

People / process
- Named DRI per function for the pilot:
  - Product DRI: Marissa Cole
  - Release Eng DRI: Connor O’Brien
  - Runtime DRI: Omar El-Sayed
  - SRE gate owner: Sean Gallagher
  - Support escalation owner: Dev Patel
- Support schedule: confirm on-call coverage for first two pilot patches (including one “emergency patch” drill scenario).
- Triage routing: all inbound “LTS patch request” issues tagged and routed within 1 business day.

Communication plan (cadence + templates)
Audience segments
- Pilot customers (technical + procurement stakeholders)
- Internal Support/CS (for consistent messaging)
- Internal Eng (Runtime/Release Eng/SRE)

Cadence
1) Pre-pilot briefing (T-7 days)
- Email to customer technical owner(s): what LTS is, what it is not, support window/cadence, planned cut date, required actions.
- Include links: customer-safe LTS overview, upgrade playbook, and how to open backport requests.

2) Pilot kickoff (T-0)
- 30-min call per account with Product + Release Eng + CS.
- Confirm maintenance window and rollback plan.

3) Per patch release
- “Release available” email within 24 hours of artifact publish.
- Release notes sent as a link + PDF export (some customers require attachment for change-control).
- Include: risk level, known issues, mitigations, upgrade steps, rollback steps, and support contact.

4) Weekly pilot update (first 4 weeks)
- Short email recap: what shipped (or “no changes”), upcoming patch window, any open known issues.
- Internal mirror post to #support and #eng-releases for alignment.

5) Post-pilot readout (week 6)
- 1-page summary: metrics, issues, customer feedback, and go/no-go for expanding cohort.

Comms ownership
- External emails sent by CS owner with Product CC; Product provides template and ensures consistency.
- Release notes authored by Runtime + Tech Writer; approved by Release Eng; customer-safe framing validated by Product.

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: Customers attempt to use LTS as a feature delivery channel.
  - Mitigation: “LTS eligibility” section in kickoff + strict backport policy; route feature asks to mainline.
- Risk: Patch cadence expectations mismatch.
  - Mitigation: Set explicit cadence (e.g., monthly regular + as-needed security/emergency) and define “emergency patch” criteria.
- Risk: Private installer/artifact pull friction delays upgrades.
  - Mitigation: require a dry-run on internal staging + one customer staging environment before expanding pilot.

Open questions
- Confirm whether any pilot customers require signed artifacts + SBOM delivery in a specific format (SPDX vs CycloneDX) beyond our default.
- Decide whether we offer a “customer-visible patch calendar” during pilot or keep it ad-hoc.

Next steps
- Finalize cohort list with Sales/CS and confirm NDAs + technical contacts (by 2026-01-27).
- Align with Release Eng on the first customer-facing publish date for runtime-1.20-lts.0 (target week of 2026-02-03).
- Draft external comms templates and get Support sign-off (by 2026-01-31).
- Schedule kickoff calls and maintenance windows for each account (by 2026-02-07).
